The surname Luther is from German Luther, from Old High German Liutheri (“personal name”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *Liudiharjaz, formed from *liudiz (“people”) and *harjaz (“army”). 1000242.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Latin Sāturnus (“Saturn, the Roman god”), also attested in the older form Saeturnus. The Norwegian form reflects the widespread international form of the name without the Latin ending -us.
The deeper origin of the Latin name is uncertain. Ancient Roman writers connected it with satus (“sown”), the past participle of serō (“to sow, plant”), in reference to Saturn's association with agriculture. 1004594.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Surkudalr (“Surka valley”), from the genitive of the river name *Surka and dalr (“valley”). The river, now called Sørkedalselva, formerly bore the name Surka. The river name is of uncertain origin; it may be related to Proto-Germanic *swerkaną (“to become dark”), which would give the meaning “the dark one”, or be sound-symbolic, compare surkle (“to gurgle, squelch”).
Compare the Norwegian river names Sorka, Svarka, Sverka and Svorka, which have been assigned to the same name group.

1005106.etyen:
Compound of forsvinning (“disappearance, vanishing”) + drakt (“suit, outfit”), literally “disappearance suit”.
The first element forsvinning (“disappearance, vanishing”) is the verbal noun of forsvinne (“to disappear, vanish”), formed with -ing (“action/result-forming noun suffix”). The verb is derived from Middle Low German vorswinden (“to disappear, vanish”); its prefix ultimately reflects Proto-West Germanic *fra- (“verbal prefix”), while its second element continues Old Saxon swindan (“to diminish, dwindle”), from Proto-West Germanic *swindan (“to diminish, dwindle”).
